Notes from a week without a phone

I left my phone in a drawer for seven days and kept a paper diary of what changed. The first two days were restless. I reached for a pocket that was empty a dozen times before lunch.

By the fourth day the reaching had faded. I noticed how long a bus ride really takes, and how many people on it were looking at screens. I read half a novel on the commute.

The practical problems were small but real. I missed one message about a change of meeting room and had to ask a stranger for directions. Neither was a disaster.

I would not give up the phone for good. I did put a time limit on the apps that took the most hours, and the drawer is still where it goes at dinner.
